title: Flat maps that are isomorphisms modulo I are isomorphisms modulo all powers of I
statement: Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a flat ring map of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal; write $I^nB$ for the ideal of $B$ generated by $\varphi(I^n)$. Assume that the ring map $A/I\to B/IB$ induced by $\varphi$ is an isomorphism. Then for every $n\ge1$ the ring map $A/I^n\to B/I^nB$ induced by $\varphi$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0AGU (lemma-henselization-flat, line 3105): 'Since each $A\to B$ is flat we find that the maps $A/I^n\to B/I^nB$ are isomorphisms as well (for example by Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-lift-basis})', i.e. Algebra Lemma Tag 051H (lemma-lift-basis, algebra.tex line 24343) applied to $R=A/I^n$, the nilpotent ideal $I/I^n$, $M=B/I^nB$ and the single element $1$ (Tor-vanishing by flatness of $B$ over $A$)

proof.text: *Set-up.* For $n\ge1$ let $\beta_n:A/I^n\to B/I^nB$, $a\bmod I^n\mapsto\varphi(a)\bmod I^nB$; it is well defined since $\varphi(I^n)\subseteq I^nB$, it is a ring map, and it is $A$-linear for the $A$-module structures through $A\to A/I^n$ and $\varphi$. Since $I^{n+1}\subseteq I^n$ and $I^{n+1}B\subseteq I^nB$, the third isomorphism theorem gives short exact sequences of $A$-modules $0\to I^n/I^{n+1}\xrightarrow{\iota}A/I^{n+1}\xrightarrow{\pi}A/I^n\to0$ and $0\to I^nB/I^{n+1}B\xrightarrow{\iota'}B/I^{n+1}B\xrightarrow{\pi'}B/I^nB\to0$ (inclusion and reduction). Let $\alpha_n:I^n/I^{n+1}\to I^nB/I^{n+1}B$, $x\bmod I^{n+1}\mapsto\varphi(x)\bmod I^{n+1}B$ (well defined since $\varphi(I^n)\subseteq I^nB$, $\varphi(I^{n+1})\subseteq I^{n+1}B$). All maps are induced by $\varphi$, so $\iota'\circ\alpha_n=\beta_{n+1}\circ\iota$ and $\pi'\circ\beta_{n+1}=\beta_n\circ\pi$: the two rows with vertical maps $\alpha_n,\beta_{n+1},\beta_n$ form a commutative diagram of $A$-modules.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0AGU (lemma-henselization-flat, lines 3101-3104), which refers to Algebra Lemma Tag 051H (lemma-lift-basis, algebra.tex lines 24342-24384); the induction below is the argument of the proof of 051H for the single element $1$, written as an induction on $n$

proof.text: *$\alpha_n$ is surjective.* Since $\beta_1$ is surjective, $B=\varphi(A)+IB$. The ideal $I^nB$ is additively generated by the products $\varphi(x)b$ with $x\in I^n$, $b\in B$. Write $b=\varphi(a)+y$ with $a\in A$, $y\in IB$; then $\varphi(x)b=\varphi(xa)+\varphi(x)y$ with $xa\in I^n$ and $\varphi(x)y\in I^nB\cdot IB\subseteq I^{n+1}B$. Hence $I^nB=\varphi(I^n)+I^{n+1}B$, i.e. $\alpha_n$ is surjective.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0AGU (lemma-henselization-flat, lines 3101-3104), which refers to Algebra Lemma Tag 051H (lemma-lift-basis, algebra.tex lines 24342-24384); the induction below is the argument of the proof of 051H for the single element $1$, written as an induction on $n$

proof.text: *$\alpha_n$ is injective (flatness).* Put $N=I^n/I^{n+1}$, an $A$-module annihilated by $I$. (a) The map $j:N\to N\otimes_AB$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, is injective: let $\psi=\beta_1^{-1}:B/IB\to A/I$, an $A$-linear ring isomorphism. The map $N\times B\to N$, $(x,b)\mapsto\psi(b\bmod IB)\cdot x$ (with $N$ an $A/I$-module) is $A$-bilinear, so it induces an $A$-linear $r:N\otimes_AB\to N$ with $r(x\otimes b)=\psi(\bar b)x$; then $r(j(x))=\psi(1)x=x$, so $r\circ j=\mathrm{id}_N$. (b) Since $B$ is a flat $A$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and $\iota:N\to A/I^{n+1}$ is injective, $\iota\otimes\mathrm{id}_B:N\otimes_AB\to(A/I^{n+1})\otimes_AB$ is injective. (c) Composing with the swap $(A/I^{n+1})\otimes_AB\cong B\otimes_A(A/I^{n+1})$ and the isomorphism $B\otimes_A(A/I^{n+1})\xrightarrow{\sim}B/I^{n+1}B$, $b\otimes\bar a\mapsto\varphi(a)b$ [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change, applied to the ideal $I^{n+1}$], we get an injective $A$-linear map $\mu:N\otimes_AB\to B/I^{n+1}B$ with $\mu(\bar x\otimes b)=\varphi(x)b\bmod I^{n+1}B$. (d) For $x\in I^n$, $\mu(j(\bar x))=\varphi(x)\bmod I^{n+1}B=\iota'(\alpha_n(\bar x))$. So $\iota'\circ\alpha_n=\mu\circ j$ is injective, hence $\alpha_n$ is injective.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0AGU (lemma-henselization-flat, lines 3101-3104), which refers to Algebra Lemma Tag 051H (lemma-lift-basis, algebra.tex lines 24342-24384); the induction below is the argument of the proof of 051H for the single element $1$, written as an induction on $n$

proof.text: *Induction.* We show by induction on $n\ge1$ that $\beta_n$ is bijective. For $n=1$ this is the hypothesis. If $\beta_n$ is bijective, then in the commutative diagram of step 1, whose rows are short exact sequences in the abelian category of $A$-modules, $\alpha_n$ is an isomorphism (steps 2 and 3) and $\beta_n$ is an isomorphism, so $\beta_{n+1}$ is an isomorphism by the short five lemma [lem-weil-pbc-short-five-lemma]. A bijective ring map is a ring isomorphism (its set-theoretic inverse is additive and multiplicative), so $A/I^n\to B/I^nB$ is an isomorphism of rings for every $n\ge1$.
